The most underrated city in Africa 🇩🇿 Oran is the second largest city in Algeria, known for its Mediterranean coastline, beautiful architecture, vibrant cafe culture, incredible food, and raï music. This city has a real charm to it and everyone needs to visit it once in their life. #oran #algeria #travelalgeria #africa #solotravel

After weeks in a strict, conservative country, one city felt like a different world 🇩🇿 Oran is open, artistic and free. Women work as doctors, lawyers, in government, and I saw women serving in a restaurant without a hijab for the first time on the trip. A port city that chose to be free. 👇 #oran #algeria #progressive #northafrica #travel #mediterranean

From a beach in California, the conversation came back to Algeria. 🇩🇿🌊 She came as a visitor. What stayed with her wasn’t just the landscapes, the food or the history. It was the people. That’s the thing about Algeria: some of what makes it unforgettable is difficult to explain until you’ve experienced it yourself. So let’s ask the people who know it best: What’s ONE thing about Algeria you wish the rest of the world understood? 🇩🇿 Tell us below — especially if you’re Algerian or part of the diaspora. And if there’s someone in your DMs who only knows the Algeria they’ve seen from afar, send them this. Some places impress you. Algeria stays with you. Not travel. A return. #Algeria #الجزائر #Algerie #TravelStories #Wanderlust

videos.caption: My final thoughts before leaving Algeria 🇩🇿❤️ After traveling through the country, I can honestly say Algeria is one of those places that’s hard to fully understand until you experience it yourself. It’s incredibly underrated and has some of the best people in the world. The hospitality, culture, food, and everything I experienced here made this trip truly special. Thank you Algeria, until next time. ❤️🇩🇿 #algeria #solotravel

Attending my first Algerian wedding 🇩🇿 This is what a wedding looks like in the Kabylie mountains of Algeria! 🏔️🇩🇿 One of the most unique weddings I’ve ever attended in my life. #algeria #solotravel #algerian

Places in Algeria that don’t feel real. 🇩🇿 The endless red dunes and towering rock formations of Tadrart. The remarkably preserved Roman ruins of Djemila, surrounded by mountains. The lush green forests of Seraïdi, overlooking the Mediterranean. And Constantine, a city built dramatically across cliffs and deep gorges, connected by bridges suspended high above the landscape. If Tadrart is on your list, you can experience it with  @duneyatours, our Tuareg-owned and operated agency based in Djanet. Travel deep into the Sahara by 4×4, camp beneath the stars, discover ancient rock art and experience the desert alongside the people who have travelled these lands for generations.
